events.title: Master of Arts in Teaching Information Session
events.description:
Have you ever considered teaching? If so, please join us for an information session on Wednesday, October 21 from 3:30 – 4:30 PM to learn more about SMC’s one-year Master of Arts in Teaching (MAT) program. This competitively-priced program is open to students from any major. No prior education coursework is required. The MAT leads to a master’s degree and licensure in art, elementary, middle, secondary, or special education. SMC juniors and seniors can take up to 3 graduate courses as part of their undergraduate program at no additional cost and save up to $6,000 in graduate tuition. The program is also open to graduates of other colleges and universities.
Visit smcvt.edu/gradevents to register. To learn more about the MAT, visit smcvt.edu/mat or contact Amy Saks Pavese at [contact omitted].

events.title: Graduate Education Open House
events.description: Join us to learn more about the Graduate Education programs at Saint Michael’s College, meet current faculty and students, and attend a graduate class. Designed to support educators at all stages of their professional journey from pre-service teacher to experienced school leader, SMC offers the following programs: Master of Arts in Teaching, Master of Education, post-master’s Certificate of Advanced Graduate Study, and Graduate Certificates, with options for initial teacher licensure and additional endorsements in school leadership. Our newly redesigned M.Ed. and C.A.G.S. programs now offer four new concentrations with more options for personalization, applied learning, online courses, and flexibility. Come learn how SMC can support you in meeting your professional goals.

events.title: Artist Talk: Lucia Monge
events.description:
Visiting artist Lucia Monge will be talking about her work and her exhibition in the McCarthy Art Gallery, “Against the Grain.” The talk will be in Saint Edmund’s Hall 104.

Artist bio
Lucia Monge is a Peruvian artist whose work explores the ways humans position ourselves
within the natural world and relate to other living beings, especially plants. Some of her
recent projects include exploring interspecies vulnerability and material circularity through
plant respiration, a “fungi broadcast” about deforestation in the Amazon, sending potato
seeds to space as messengers for non-colonial visions of space travel, and organizing
“walking forest” performances that have led to the creation of green spaces in Lima,
London, New York, Paris, and Pamplona.
Monge has shown her work internationally, including at the Museum of Latin American Art,
Queens Museum, Whitechapel Gallery, Museum of Contemporary Art in Lima, the United
Nations Climate Change Conference, Ars Electronica, and the Havana and Shenzhen
biennales. She has received grants from the Oak Spring Garden Foundation, Peruvian
Ministry of Culture, COAL, and Foundation for Contemporary Arts, among other. Her work
has been featured in publications such as MoMA’s Uneven Growth, Global Performance
Studies, Let’s Become Fungal, The Work of Art in the Age of Planetary Destruction, and
Lejos de la Tierra, among other.
She holds an MFA from Rhode Island School of Design and a BFA from Universidad
Católica del Perú. She is a founding member of FIBRA art collective, and Assistant
Professor of Art at Amherst College.

events.title: McCarthy Art Gallery Reception: “Against the Grain” an exhibition by Lucia Monge
events.description: Please join us at a gallery reception for visiting artist Lucia Monge’s exhibition “Against the Grain,” a sculptural installation focused on Amaranthus palmeri, a plant that some call a “superfood” and others a “superweed.” It has evolved to resist at least six herbicides used to support GMO monoculture. The installation sets a large-scale amaranth ovary against a homogeneous field of corn and soy, to explore classification, exploitation, and resistance.

events.title: The Branching Out Symposium
events.description:
Join us for the Leahy Institute for Environment’s annual Branching Out Symposium—an evening of presentations and celebrations focused on Teaching, Learning, and Leadership in, for, and about the environment. The event will be held Thursday, November 12th from 5:00–8:00 p.m. in the Dion Center’s Roy Room.

Our goal is to uplift the work of I4E students and highlight the many ways we learn about and care for the world—across fields, disciplines, and lived experiences. The event will feature light networking, food drinks, guest speakers, and student poster presentations.
